title: Dependency safety harness and phased diversion protocol
creator: Asha Nair
description: Goal: Build a low-risk, testable 'safety harness' that sits above per-dependency/per-model/per-tenant routing and performs calibrated detection, phased diversion, and graceful degraded responses. This harness should: 1) compute SLO-aligned trip signals using latency quantiles and error ratios on moving windows, 2) apply region-aware hysteresis and a phased diversion protocol (partial diversion -> staged increase -> full diversion) to avoid noisy flips, 3) coordinate safe fallbacks (cache returns, best-effort stub model, informative degradation messages) and per-tenant budgeted shedding, and 4) emit rich events for the Console (rollouts page) and Grafana for post-incident analysis. We will prioritize predictable customer-visible behavior over optimizing immediate throughput during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Safety harness can be attached to any model or dependency via config flag and policy reference. 2) Phased diversion has three levels (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with configurable hold windows and hysteresis. 3) Diversions are region-aware and can be limited by tenant SLA tiers. 4) Fallbacks documented and implemented: cache response, contextual degraded stub (explainability tag), and last-success snapshot. 5) End-to-end e2e tests and an integration demo that triggers a predictable diversion for a synthetic latency spike. 6) Console shows per-diversion traces and cost delta for diverted traffic.
design_notes: We avoid a binary open/closed fuse. Instead of a single threshold, the harness uses a composite score: 60% weight on p95 latency relative to SLO, 30% on error-rate spike over baseline, 10% on capacity headroom. Thresholds are tiered by tenant (gold/silver/bronze). Hold windows default to 30s at first stage, 2m at second, and 10m at third. Backoff on recovery uses exponential decay with min hold to avoid oscillation. For fallbacks, prefer cached outputs when prefix matches; otherwise call a lightweight stateless stub (smaller, quantized model) with a flagged response that includes a "degraded" provenance header so downstream can surface an explanation. All decisions must be auditable in the Console and retained for 30 days.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): instrumentation and composite score calculation; add config hooks to routing layer; unit tests for score heuristics. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement staged diversion mechanics and hysteresis; integrate tenant-tier caps; add metrics and event schema. Phase 3 (1 week): implement fallback strategies (cache lookup, stub model path, last-success snapshot); add e2e test harness. Phase 4 (1 week): Console integration (events + trace links), canary rollout to a small set of non-critical tenants, collect metrics. Phase 5: post-canary adjustments and wide rollout. Rollback plan: instant disable flag at control plane; safe gradual rollback by reversing staged diversion steps.
tradeoffs:
- Using a composite score improves stability but requires tuning weights per workload; initial weights are conservative to avoid unnecessary diversion.
- Staged diversion reduces customer impact but increases implementation complexity and testing surface.
- Favoring cached/stub responses keeps latency low but reduces output fidelity (must be surfaced to users).
- Tenant-tier caps protect revenue-critical customers but add policy complexity to routing decisions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for score calc and hysteresis; synthetic chaos tests injecting latency/error bursts in test clusters; integration test that simulates multi-region failover and verifies diversion progression and fallback response headers; load test to validate cost delta when diversion enabled; canary with 5 tenants for 48h observing SLOs and Console events.
metrics_and_observability: Emit: composite_score, diversion_stage, diversion_reason, diverted_percent, fallback_type, tenant_tier, region. Dashboards: dependency-health (per model/dependency), diversion-playbook (stages over time), tenant-exposure (who hit diversions). Alerting: when composite_score > stage-2 threshold for 3 consecutive windows trigger P0 ops alert; when fallback_type == stub_model for >5% global QPS trigger investigation. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd123/dependency-health
